text:
The new residents are projected to settle primarily in Hardin.

Lodge Grass has not been affected by Westmoreland Resources because the distance is large, the roads are poor, and winter weather makes traveling very difficult. This is expected to continue unless coal is developed to the east or south, in which case the town would experience some growth from this cause. If this does not occur, facility and service demands in Lodge Grass will be determined primarily by natural population increases.
Big Horn County has experienced beneficial effects from existing coal development. Increased revenue from higher levels of taxable valuation accrues to the county government, as does four percent of the state's receipts from the Coal Severance Tax on coal within the county's boundaries. Some increase in demands for services has been experienced; however, these have been relatively small. In general, the effects of coal mining have been beneficial for the county government, and the County Clerk expects this will continue to be the case (personal communication, January 8, 1976).
The effects of coal mining have been very different for the city of Hardin. The City Clerk feels that the coal development by Westmoreland caused an influx of people into the city, resulting in a strain on the provision of city services, particularly water and sewer services. The services must be increased during construction phases, but when the impact of the construction phase is over, many of the newly-provided services may be left unused and will not collect revenue (City Clerk, January 8, 1976).
